verses.zh: 这月二十四日，以色列人聚集禁食，身穿麻衣，头蒙灰尘。
verses.en: On the twenty-fourth day of this same month the Israelites assembled; they were fasting and wearing sackcloth, their heads covered with dust.

verses.zh: 以色列人（人：原文是种类）就与一切外邦人离绝，站着承认自己的罪恶和列祖的罪孽。
verses.en: Those truly of Israelite descent[NOTE:1] separated from all the foreigners,[NOTE:2] standing and confessing their sins and the iniquities of their ancestors.[NOTE:3]

verses.zh: 那日的四分之一站在自己的地方念耶和华―他们　神的律法书，又四分之一认罪，敬拜耶和华―他们的　神。
verses.en: For one-fourth of the day they stood in their place and read from the book of the law of the Lord their God, and for another fourth they were confessing their sins[NOTE:1] and worshiping the Lord their God.
notes: Heb “confessing.” The words “their sins” are not present in the Hebrew text of v. 3, but are clearly implied here because they are explicitly stated in v. 2.

verses.zh: 耶书亚、巴尼、甲篾、示巴尼、布尼、示利比、巴尼、基拿尼站在利未人的台上，大声哀求耶和华―他们的　神。
verses.en: Then the Levites—Jeshua, Binnui,[NOTE:1] Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Kenani—stood on the steps and called out loudly[NOTE:2] to the Lord their God.
notes: Heb “Bani.” The translation reads “Binnui” (so also NAB) rather than the MT reading “Bani.” Otherwise there are two individuals with the same name in this verse. The name “Binnui” appears, for example, in Neh 10:10.

verses.zh: 利未人耶书亚、甲篾、巴尼、哈沙尼、示利比、荷第雅、示巴尼、毗他希雅说：「你们要站起来称颂耶和华―你们的　神，永世无尽。耶和华啊，你荣耀之名是应当称颂的！超乎一切称颂和赞美。」
verses.en: The Levites—Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah—said, “Stand up and bless the Lord your God!”“May you be blessed, O Lord our God, from age to age.[NOTE:1] May your glorious name[NOTE:2] be blessed; may it be lifted up above all blessing and praise.
notes: The MT reads here only “from age to age,” without the preceding words “May you be blessed, O LORD our God” which are included in the present translation. But apparently something has dropped out of the text. This phrase occurs elsewhere in the OT as a description of the Lord (see Pss 41:13; 106:48), and it seems best to understand it here in that light. The LXX adds “And Ezra said” at the beginning of v. 6 as a transition: “And Ezra said, ‘You alone are the LORD.” Without this addition (which is not included by most modern English translations) the speakers of vv. 9:5b-10:1 continue to be the Levites of v. 5a.

verses.zh: 「你，惟独你是耶和华！你造了天和天上的天，并天上的万象，地和地上的万物，海和海中所有的；这一切都是你所保存的。天军也都敬拜你。
verses.en: You alone are the Lord. You made the heavens, even the highest heavens,[NOTE:1] along with all their multitude of stars,[NOTE:2] the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them. You impart life to them all, and the multitudes of heaven worship you.

verses.zh: 你是耶和华　神，曾拣选亚伯兰，领他出迦勒底的吾珥，给他改名叫亚伯拉罕。
verses.en: “You are the Lord God who chose Abram and brought him forth from Ur of the Chaldeans. You changed his name to Abraham.

verses.zh: 你见他在你面前心里诚实，就与他立约，应许把迦南人、赫人、亚摩利人、比利洗人、耶布斯人、革迦撒人之地赐给他的后裔，且应验了你的话，因为你是公义的。
verses.en: When you perceived that his heart was faithful toward you, you established a[NOTE:1] covenant with him to give his descendants[NOTE:2] the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites. You have fulfilled your promise,[NOTE:3] for you are righteous.

verses.zh: 「你曾看见我们列祖在埃及所受的困苦，垂听他们在红海边的哀求，
verses.en: “You saw the affliction of our ancestors in Egypt, and you heard their cry at the Red Sea.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the Sea of Reeds.” Traditionally this is identified as the Red Sea, and the modern designation has been used in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 就施行神迹奇事在法老和他一切臣仆，并他国中的众民身上。你也得了名声，正如今日一样，因为你知道他们向我们列祖行事狂傲。
verses.en: You performed awesome signs[NOTE:1] against Pharaoh, against his servants, and against all the people of his land, for you knew that the Egyptians[NOTE:2] had acted presumptuously[NOTE:3] against them. You made for yourself a name that is celebrated to this day.
notes: Heb “signs and wonders.” This phrase is a hendiadys. The second noun functions adjectivally, while the first noun retains its full nominal sense: “awesome signs” or “miraculous signs.”
Heb “they”; the referent (the Egyptians) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 你又在我们列祖面前把海分开，使他们在海中行走干地，将追赶他们的人抛在深海，如石头抛在大水中；
verses.en: You split the sea before them, and they crossed through[NOTE:1] the sea on dry ground. But you threw their pursuers[NOTE:2] into the depths, like a stone into surging[NOTE:3] waters.

verses.zh: 并且白昼用云柱引导他们，黑夜用火柱照亮他们当行的路。
verses.en: You guided them with a pillar of cloud by day and with a pillar of fire by night to illumine for them the path they were to travel.

verses.zh: 你也降临在西奈山，从天上与他们说话，赐给他们正直的典章、真实的律法、美好的条例与诫命，
verses.en: “You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You provided them with just judgments, true laws, and good statutes and commandments.

verses.zh: 又使他们知道你的安息圣日，并藉你仆人摩西传给他们诫命、条例、律法。
verses.en: You made known to them your holy Sabbath; you issued commandments, statutes, and laws to them through[NOTE:1] Moses your servant.

verses.zh: 从天上赐下粮食充他们的饥，从磐石使水流出解他们的渴，又吩咐他们进去得你起誓应许赐给他们的地。
verses.en: You provided bread from heaven for them in their time of hunger, and you brought forth water from the rock for them in their time of thirst. You told them to enter in order to possess the land that you had sworn[NOTE:1] to give them.

verses.zh: 但我们的列祖行事狂傲，硬着颈项不听从你的诫命；
verses.en: “But they—our ancestors[NOTE:1]—behaved presumptuously; they rebelled[NOTE:2] and did not obey your commandments.
notes: Heb “and our fathers.” The ו (vav) is explicative.
Heb “they stiffened their neck” (so also in the following verse).

verses.zh: 不肯顺从，也不记念你在他们中间所行的奇事，竟硬着颈项，居心背逆，自立首领，要回他们为奴之地。但你是乐意饶恕人，有恩典，有怜悯，不轻易发怒，有丰盛慈爱的　神，并不丢弃他们。
verses.en: They refused to obey and did not recall your miracles that you had performed among them. Instead, they rebelled and appointed a leader to return to their bondage in Egypt.[NOTE:1] But you are a God of forgiveness, merciful and compassionate, slow to get angry and unfailing in your loyal love.[NOTE:2] You did not abandon them,
notes: The present translation follows a few medieval Hebrew MSS and the LXX in reading בְּמִצְרָיִם (bemitsrayim, “in Egypt”; so also NAB, NASB, NRSV, TEV, NLT) rather than the MT reading בְּמִרְיָם (bemiryam, “in their rebellion”).
The translation follows the Qere reading חֶסֶד (khesed, “loyal love”) rather than the Kethib reading וְחֶסֶד (vekhesed, “and loyal love”) of the MT.

verses.zh: 他们虽然铸了一只牛犊，彼此说『这是领你出埃及的　神』，因而大大惹动你的怒气；
verses.en: even when they made a cast image of a calf for themselves and said, ‘This is your God who brought you up from Egypt,’ or when they committed atrocious[NOTE:1] blasphemies.

verses.zh: 你还是大施怜悯，在旷野不丢弃他们。白昼，云柱不离开他们，仍引导他们行路；黑夜，火柱也不离开他们，仍照亮他们当行的路。
verses.en: “Due to your great compassion you did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not stop guiding them in the path by day,[NOTE:1] nor did the pillar of fire stop illuminating for them by night the path on which they should travel.
notes: Heb “did not turn from them by day to guide them in the path.”

verses.zh: 你也赐下你良善的灵教训他们；未尝不赐吗哪使他们糊口，并赐水解他们的渴。
verses.en: You imparted your good Spirit to instruct them. You did not withhold your manna from their mouths; you provided water for their thirst.

verses.zh: 在旷野四十年，你养育他们，他们就一无所缺：衣服没有穿破，脚也没有肿。
verses.en: For 40 years you sustained them. Even in the wilderness they never lacked anything. Their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell.

verses.zh: 并且你将列国之地照分赐给他们，他们就得了西宏之地、希实本王之地，和巴珊王噩之地。
verses.en: “You gave them kingdoms and peoples, and you allocated them to every corner of the land.[NOTE:1] They inherited the land of King Sihon of Heshbon[NOTE:2] and the land of King Og of Bashan.
notes: The words “of the land” are not in the Hebrew text, but are supplied in the translation for clarity.

Most Hebrew MSS read “the land of Sihon and the land of the king of Heshbon.” The present translation (along with NAB, NASB, NIV, NCV, NRSV, CEV, NLT) follows the reading of one Hebrew MS, the LXX, and the Vulgate.

verses.zh: 你也使他们的子孙多如天上的星，带他们到你所应许他们列祖进入得为业之地。
verses.en: You multiplied their descendants like the stars of the sky. You brought them to the land you had told their ancestors to enter in order to possess.

verses.zh: 这样，他们进去得了那地，你在他们面前制伏那地的居民，就是迦南人；将迦南人和其君王，并那地的居民，都交在他们手里，让他们任意而待。
verses.en: Their descendants[NOTE:1] entered and possessed the land. You subdued before them the Canaanites who were the inhabitants of the land. You delivered them into their hand, together with their kings and the peoples of the land, to deal with as they pleased.

verses.zh: 他们得了坚固的城邑、肥美的地土、充满各样美物的房屋、凿成的水井、葡萄园、橄榄园，并许多果木树。他们就吃而得饱，身体肥胖，因你的大恩，心中快乐。
verses.en: They captured fortified cities and fertile land. They took possession of houses full of all sorts of good things—wells previously dug, vineyards, olive trees, and fruit trees in abundance. They ate until they were full[NOTE:1] and grew fat. They enjoyed to the full your great goodness.
notes: Heb “they ate and were sated.” This expression is a hendiadys. The first verb retains its full verbal sense, while the second functions adverbially: “they ate and were filled” = “they ate until they were full.”

verses.zh: 「然而，他们不顺从，竟背叛你，将你的律法丢在背后，杀害那劝他们归向你的众先知，大大惹动你的怒气。
verses.en: “Nonetheless they grew disobedient and rebelled against you; they disregarded your law.[NOTE:1] They killed your prophets who had solemnly admonished them in order to cause them to return to you. They committed atrocious blasphemies.
notes: Heb “they cast your law behind their backs.”

verses.zh: 所以你将他们交在敌人的手中，磨难他们。他们遭难的时候哀求你，你就从天上垂听，照你的大怜悯赐给他们拯救者，救他们脱离敌人的手。
verses.en: Therefore you delivered them into the hand of their adversaries, who oppressed them. But in the time of their distress they called to you, and you heard from heaven. In your abundant compassion you provided them with deliverers to rescue them from[NOTE:1] their adversaries.
notes: Heb “from the hand of” (so NASB, NIV); NAB “from the power of.”

verses.zh: 但他们得平安之后，又在你面前行恶，所以你丢弃他们在仇敌的手中，使仇敌辖制他们。然而他们转回哀求你，你仍从天上垂听，屡次照你的怜悯拯救他们，
verses.en: “Then, when they were at rest again, they went back to doing evil before you. Then you abandoned them to[NOTE:1] their enemies, and they gained dominion over them. When they again cried out to you, in your compassion you heard from heaven and rescued them time and again.
notes: Heb “in the hand of” (so KJV, ASV); NAB “to the power of.”

verses.zh: 又警戒他们，要使他们归服你的律法。他们却行事狂傲，不听从你的诫命，干犯你的典章（人若遵行就必因此活着），扭转肩头，硬着颈项，不肯听从。
verses.en: And you solemnly admonished them in order to return them to your law, but they behaved presumptuously and did not obey your commandments. They sinned against your ordinances—those by which an individual, if he obeys them,[NOTE:1] will live. They boldly turned from you;[NOTE:2] they rebelled[NOTE:3] and did not obey.
notes: Heb “if a man keep.” See note on the word “obey” in Neh 1:5.

verses.zh: 但你多年宽容他们，又用你的灵藉众先知劝戒他们，他们仍不听从，所以你将他们交在列国之民的手中。
verses.en: You prolonged your kindness[NOTE:1] with them for many years, and you solemnly admonished them by your Spirit through your prophets. Still they paid no attention,[NOTE:2] so you delivered them into the hands of the neighboring peoples.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew expression here is elliptical. The words “your kindness” are not included in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 然而你大发怜悯，不全然灭绝他们，也不丢弃他们；因为你是有恩典、有怜悯的　神。
verses.en: However, due to your abundant mercy you did not do away with them altogether; you did not abandon them. For you are a merciful and compassionate God.

verses.zh: 「我们的　神啊，你是至大、至能、至可畏、守约施慈爱的　神。我们的君王、首领、祭司、先知、列祖，和你的众民，从亚述列王的时候直到今日所遭遇的苦难，现在求你不要以为小。
verses.en: “So now, our God—the great, powerful, and awesome God, who keeps covenant fidelity[NOTE:1]—do not regard as inconsequential[NOTE:2] all the hardship that has befallen us—our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors, and all your people—from the days of the kings of Assyria until this very day.
notes: Heb “the covenant and loyal love.” The expression is a hendiadys. The second noun retains its full nominal sense, while the first functions adjectivally: “the covenant and loyalty” = covenant fidelity.
Heb “do not let it seem small in your sight.”

verses.zh: 在一切临到我们的事上，你却是公义的；因你所行的是诚实，我们所做的是邪恶。
verses.en: You are righteous with regard to all that has happened to us, for you have acted faithfully.[NOTE:1] It is we who have been in the wrong!

verses.zh: 我们的君王、首领、祭司、列祖都不遵守你的律法，不听从你的诫命和你警戒他们的话。
verses.en: Our kings, our leaders, our priests, and our ancestors have not kept your law. They have not paid attention to your commandments or your testimonies by which you have solemnly admonished them.

verses.zh: 他们在本国里沾你大恩的时候，在你所赐给他们这广大肥美之地上不事奉你，也不转离他们的恶行。
verses.en: Even when they were in their kingdom and benefiting from your incredible[NOTE:1] goodness that you had lavished[NOTE:2] on them in the spacious and fertile land you had set[NOTE:3] before them, they did not serve you, nor did they turn from their evil practices.

verses.zh: 我们现今作了奴仆；至于你所赐给我们列祖享受其上的土产，并美物之地，看哪，我们在这地上作了奴仆！
verses.en: “So today we are slaves! In the very land you gave to our ancestors to eat its fruit and to enjoy[NOTE:1] its good things—we are slaves.
notes: The expression “to enjoy” is not included in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 这地许多出产归了列王，就是你因我们的罪所派辖制我们的。他们任意辖制我们的身体和牲畜，我们遭了大难。」
verses.en: Its abundant produce goes to the kings you have placed over us due to our sins. They rule over our bodies and our livestock as they see fit,[NOTE:1] and we are in great distress!

verses.zh: 因这一切的事，我们立确实的约，写在册上。我们的首领、利未人，和祭司都签了名。
verses.en: (10:1)[NOTE:1] “Because of all this we are entering into[NOTE:2] a binding covenant in written form;[NOTE:3] our leaders, our Levites, and our priests have affixed their names[NOTE:4] on the sealed document.”
notes: Beginning with 9:38, the verse numbers through 10:39 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 9:38 ET = 10:1 HT, 10:1 ET = 10:2 HT, 10:2 ET = 10:3 HT, etc., through 10:39 ET = 10:40 HT. Beginning with 11:1 the verse numbers in the ET and HT are again the same.

Heb “our leaders, our Levites, and our priests on the sealed document.” The Hebrew text is elliptical here; the words “have affixed their names” are supplied in the translation for clarity and for stylistic reasons. Cf. v. 2.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Third paragraph, etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

A. Nehemiah's summary of YHWH's gracious acts and covenant faithfulness (cf. Neh. 9:17) may have come from Ezra's reading of the Book of Moses (i.e., Pentateuch).

B. The chapter outlines as

1. YHWH as creator (Gen. 1-11), Neh. 9:6

2. YHWH's choice of Abraham (Gen. 12-50), Neh. 9:7-8

3. YHWH's actions in the Exodus (Exodus), Neh. 9:9-14

4. YHWH's faithful care and provision during the wilderness wandering period (Numbers), Neh. 9:15-21

5. YHWH's promises to Abraham fulfilled (period of the conquest, i.e., Joshua), Neh. 9:22-25

6. Israel's further rebellion (period of the Judges), Neh. 9:26-31

7. YHWH's covenant faithfulness and Israel's unfaithfulness continue (the period of the Monarchy), Neh. 9:32-38

C. Nehemiah 9 shows the theological basis of Israel's history - YHWH's faithfulness to His covenant; Israel's unfaithfulness to His covenant. It was not YHWH's powerlessness, but Israel's sin that brought destruction and exile; however, it is
because of YHWH's character and power that Israel exists and is back in the
Promised Land!

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: NEHEMIAH 9:1-4

1Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month the sons of Israel assembled with fasting, in sackcloth and with dirt upon them. 2The descendants of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners, and stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers. 3While they stood in their place, they read from the book of the law of the Lord their God for a fourth of the day; and for another fourth they confessed and worshiped the Lord their God. 4Now on the Levites' platform stood Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani and Chenani, and they cried with a loud voice to the Lord their God.

9:1 "on the twenty-fourth day of this month, the sons of Israel assembled with fasting, in sackcloth, with
dirt upon them" Two days after the Feast of the Booths (cf. Neh. 8:13-18) and twenty-three days after the
reading of the law (cf. Neh. 8:2), the repentant actions so characteristic of the Day of Atonement
(cf. Leviticus 16, which was to be observed on the 10th day) occurred (cf. Neh. 1:4). During the
reading of the law these returnees felt these same feelings of remorse and guilt (cf. Neh. 8:9). Israel
needed forgiveness as the rest of chapter 9 clearly shows. Their covenant God was faithful (cf. Ezra 9:8-9),
but they were not (cf. Neh. 1:6; Ezra 9:6-7,10).

▣ "fasting, in sackcloth" See
Special Topic: Grieving Rites.

9:2 "descendants of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners" This VERB (BDB 95,
KB 110, Niphal IMPERFECT) means "to withdraw from," "separate ourselves from." This
withdrawal was for the stated purpose of obeying YHWH's commands (cf. Exod. 33:16; Lev. 20:24,26;
Ezra 6:21; 9:1; 10:1). To worship and obey YHWH meant a complete break with the pagan and semi-pagan
culture and practices (cf. Lev. 20:24,26; e.g., marriages to foreign women).

▣ "confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers" This VERB (BDB 392,
KB 389 II, Hithpael IMPERFECT) means "to confess" (cf. Lev. 5:5; 16:21; Ezra 10:1;
Neh. 1:6; Dan. 9:4,20). Apparently this confession involved personal and national sin (e.g., Lev. 26-40;
Jer. 3:25; 14:20).

9:3 "they stood in their place" This seems to refer to Neh. 8:4 (cf. Neh. 9:4).

▣ "they read from the book of the law of the Lord their God for a fourth of
the day" These returnees longed to be instructed from the Law of Moses. It seems at this point that a
major turning point in the life of the Jews occurred. Instead of being primarily people of the temple
(ritual, liturgy, and form) they became people of the Book (the influence of the synagogue). This was a
reading/teaching session lasting three hours in the morning (Bible study) and three hours in the afternoon
(confession and worship).

9:4 If Neh. 9:3 refers to Neh. 8:4, then this verse must refer to a separate platform. The names mentioned
here refer to the Levites of Neh. 8:7, who translated and interpreted Ezra's (and the men standing with him)
words.

These two groups may have been involved in antiphonal reading interspersed with translation and
interpretation.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: NEHEMIAH 9:5-8

5Then the Levites, Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah and Pethahiah, said, "Arise, bless the Lord your God forever and ever!

O may Your glorious name be blessed

And exalted above all blessing and praise!

6You alone are the Lord.

You have made the heavens,

The heaven of heavens with all their host,

The earth and all that is on it,

The seas and all that is in them.

▣ "You gave them just ordinances and true laws" There are some cultural examples similar to the
decalog.

- The Laws of Lipit-Ishtar (Sumerian), from the king of Isin (1934-1924 B.C.)

- The Laws of Eshnunna (old Babylonian), dating about 1800 B.C. from the reign
of Dadusha, king of Ashnunna

- The Code of Hammurabi (old Babylon) from the king of Babylon, Hammurabi (1728-1686 B.C.)

- The law codes of the Hittite kings Mupsilis I or Hattusilis I, from about 1650 B.C.

- The Mesopotamian law codes focus primarily on civil laws, while the biblical laws focus primarily on
religious/cultic laws. ". . .we might suggest a civil bias in all cuneiform law and a cultic bias in
Israelite law. . ., in Mesopotamia, offense is ultimately viewed in relation to society; while in Israel,
all offense is ultimately against God." Walton, p. 80.

- Albrecht Alt in Essays on Old Testament History and Religion, Oxford, 1966, pp. 81-132, has identified
two types of laws:

- casuistic, which use conditional clauses. It is characterized by an "if. . .then" structure. It
does not appeal to religious or societal norms but states a prohibition and consequence.

- apodictic, which does not use conditional clauses

(1) Exodus 21 and Deut. 27:15-26 use the third person and relate to individual,
specific cases

(2) Lev. 18:7-17 and Exodus 20/Deuteronomy 5 use the second person and are more
general in scope.

- Mesopotamian law is primarily casuistic while Israelite law is primarily apodictic.

The last two in the list are synonymous. God's power is established by His faithfulness to His
promises. These last two characteristics often appear together (cf. Neh. 1:5; 9:32; Deut. 7:2,9,12;
1 Kgs. 8:23; 2 Chr. 6:14; Dan. 9:4).

A good article on the relationship between berith (covenant) and hesed (lovingkindness)
is Edmund Jacob, Theology of the Old Testament, pp. 103-107.

Special Topic: Lovingkindness
(hesed)

▣ "From the days of the kings of Assyria to this day" Assyria took the Northern Ten Tribes
captive in 722 B.C. For a list of their kings in sequence see
Special Topic: Kings of Assyria

9:33 "You are just in all that has come upon us" The consequences for covenant violation are clearly
spelled out in Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28. God's judgments are both judicially fair and redemptively
purposeful.

9:35 "the broad and rich land" The Promised Land could hardly be characterized as "spacious," so it must
be used metaphorically for a place of freedom (cf. Exod. 3:8).

Canaan was a very fertile land in Moses' day (cf. Exod. 3:8,17; 13:5; Num. 13:23,27).

9:36 "Behold, we are slaves today" This refers to the continuing domination, albeit benevolent,
under Persia.

9:38 "We are making an agreement in writing" Although the word "covenant" is not used here, a similar
but rare word is employed. The term "agreement" is really from the Hebrew root "amen" and should be
translated "firm agreement" (BDB 53). The VERB "making" is the Hebrew term "to cut"
(BDB 503, KB 500, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE). This is often associated with the common
phrase "to cut a covenant."

9:38-10:27 "leaders. . .Levites. . .priests" The leaders are mentioned in Neh. 10:1,14-27; the Levites
in Neh. 10:9-13; and priests in Neh. 10:2-8 (cf. Neh. 12:1-7). There has been much discussion among scholars
whether individuals or families are listed. It is also unusual that Ezra is not mentioned, however, he was
a member of the first named priestly family (Seraiah).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought provoking, not definitive.

1. How are Neh. 9:1-2 related to the Day of Atonement?

2. Is confession individual or corporate or both? How does this affect the way we pray/confess today?

3. Who verbalizes the Psalm (Neh. 9:5-32)?

4. How is the group on the platform in Neh. 9:4 related to the group speaking in Neh. 9:5?

5. Outline the different periods of Israel's history alluded to in the Psalm.

6. Why is Neh. 9:17 so important?

7. Explain the OT concept of "Spirit." How do Neh. 9:20 and Neh. 9:30 relate?

8. Explain the significance of Neh. 9:31.
